hypotheses.title: Fill-Time Token Hook Bypass: ammHandleTransfer Skips _enforceTokenHooks
hypotheses.mechanism: CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer (the fill execution path called by the AMM on swap) calls ICLOBHook.validateExecutor but never calls _enforceTokenHooks. Token-level pricing bounds and handler order validation via HANDLER_ORDER_VALIDATE_FLAG are only enforced in openOrder at line 534. If an admin updates pricing bounds or pauses trading between order creation and fill execution, the fill proceeds at the original order price with no re-validation. An attacker who placed an order within the original bounds can still have it filled after bounds tighten, extracting value at a price the protocol now prohibits.
hypotheses.grounded_in: ammHandleTransfer lines 254-264 calls only ICLOBHook.validateExecutor. No call to _enforceTokenHooks exists anywhere in the fill path. Compare to openOrder line 534 which explicitly calls _enforceTokenHooks before CLOBHelper.openOrder.
hypotheses.value_extraction: Attacker places buy order at price P. Admin detects unfavorable market and raises minSqrtPrice above P. The existing CLOB order still fills at P because ammHandleTransfer never re-checks _enforceTokenHooks, giving attacker tokens at a price the protocol now considers too cheap.

hypotheses.title: computeRatioX96 Silent Overflow Returns 0 Bypasses validateHandlerOrder When Bounds Not Set
hypotheses.mechanism: SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 returns 0 (not revert) when the computed ratio exceeds uint160.max (line 51-53). In AMMStandardHook.validateHandlerOrder, this result is used to check against pricing bounds. The attack surface: a token with isSet=false (no bounds configured) but HANDLER_ORDER_VALIDATE_FLAG set — validateHandlerOrder is called and computeRatioX96 is invoked, but bounds.isSet=false means ALL price checks are skipped regardless of what the ratio computes to, including overflow. Additionally, the duplicate `if (bounds.isSet)` structure at lines 211 and 217 may create a path where the second check is dead code and intended validation is silently skipped for tokens that ARE configured.
hypotheses.grounded_in: computeRatioX96 line 52: `return 0` when tmpRatio > type(uint160).max. validateHandlerOrder calls computeRatioX96 at ~line 205 then checks bounds only if isSet=true. If isSet=false (registryUpdatePricingBounds never called), computed price is irrelevant — all orders pass regardless of how extreme the price is.
hypotheses.value_extraction: Token deployer sets HANDLER_ORDER_VALIDATE_FLAG (appears compliant) but never calls registryUpdatePricingBounds. isSet remains false. validateHandlerOrder is called for every order but performs zero price validation. Attacker can open CLOB orders at any price and have them fill against AMM liquidity at exploitative rates.

hypotheses.title: Shared tstore Slot Collision: Nested Direct Swaps Clobber beforeSwap Amount
hypotheses.mechanism: AMMStandardHook._validatePricingBounds uses a single hardcoded transient storage slot DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF for ALL direct swaps. The beforeSwap hook writes params.amount to this slot; afterSwap reads it. If a malicious token's transfer callback triggers a second direct swap before the outer swap's afterSwap executes (re-entrancy via ERC777 hook or similar), the inner beforeSwap overwrites the tstore slot. The outer afterSwap then reads the inner swap's amount and validates the outer swap's price against the wrong reference amount. An attacker controlling the inner swap amount can pass any amount they choose as the outer swap's 'before amount', making the afterSwap price check meaningless.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Single tstore slot for all direct swaps with no per-call discriminator. Call order in nested scenario: outerBeforeSwap writes X to slot → innerBeforeSwap writes Y (clobbers X) → innerAfterSwap reads Y (correct for inner) → outerAfterSwap reads Y (wrong, should be X).
hypotheses.value_extraction: Attacker uses an ERC777/ERC1363 token with transfer hook. Outer direct swap for large amount; inner direct swap triggered mid-execution for tiny amount. Outer afterSwap validates price against tiny inner amount, bypassing the actual price constraint on the large swap.

hypotheses.title: Double Rounding in calculateFixedInput Inflates amountOut, Distorts validateHandlerOrder Price Reconstruction
hypotheses.mechanism: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput applies mulDivRoundingUp TWICE: step1 = ceil(amountIn * sqrtP / Q96), then amountOut = ceil(step1 * sqrtP / Q96). Each rounding adds up to 1 wei. AMMStandardHook.validateHandlerOrder reconstructs the price from (amountOut, amountIn) via SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96. Because amountOut is inflated by double rounding, the reconstructed price is consistently higher than the actual fill price sqrtP. If maxSqrtPriceX96 == sqrtP (order at the exact maximum), the reconstructed price exceeds max and validateHandlerOrder incorrectly rejects it. Conversely, orders just below minSqrtPrice may have their reconstructed price inflated above min, making out-of-bounds fill prices appear compliant.
hypotheses.grounded_in: calculateFixedInput line 310: `amountOut = FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(amountIn, sqrtP, Q96)` then line 313: `amountOut = FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp(amountOut, sqrtP, Q96)`. Two ceil operations. validateHandlerOrder: `sqrtPriceX96 = SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96(amountOut, amountIn)`. The reconstructed price from double-rounded amountOut does not equal the original sqrtP.
hypotheses.value_extraction: Attacker opens CLOB orders with amountIn sizes chosen so that double rounding in calculateFixedInput inflates the reconstructed sqrtPrice above minSqrtPriceX96, even though the actual fill price sqrtP is below min. Orders that should be rejected are accepted.

hypotheses.title: AMM TokenSettings vs AMMStandardHook Pricing Bounds Are Separate Systems: HANDLER_ORDER_VALIDATE_FLAG Without Bounds Is Null Validation
hypotheses.mechanism: CLOBTransferHandler._enforceTokenHooks checks HANDLER_ORDER_VALIDATE_FLAG from AMM's getTokenSettings (lbamm-core TokenSettings storage at line ~590). If the flag is set, it calls AMMStandardHook.validateHandlerOrder. Inside validateHandlerOrder, pricing bounds are read from _pricingBounds[token][paired] — a separate AMMStandardHook-internal mapping. If registryUpdatePricingBounds was never called for this token, bounds.isSet = false and the entire bounds validation is skipped. A malicious token project can configure HANDLER_ORDER_VALIDATE_FLAG in the AMM (satisfying any check that looks for the flag) while never calling registryUpdatePricingBounds, ensuring all CLOB orders at any price pass validation with zero enforcement.
hypotheses.grounded_in: _enforceTokenHooks reads AMM's getTokenSettings (lbamm-core separate storage). validateHandlerOrder reads _pricingBounds[token][paired] (AMMStandardHook's own mapping). These are independent. bounds.isSet defaults to false unless registryUpdatePricingBounds is explicitly called, making validateHandlerOrder a computational no-op for any token that skips bounds configuration.
hypotheses.value_extraction: Malicious token project sets HANDLER_ORDER_VALIDATE_FLAG (signals compliance to auditors/users) while skipping registryUpdatePricingBounds configuration. All CLOB orders for their token pass validateHandlerOrder with zero restriction. Combined with fill-time bypass (H-handler-hook-01), orders at any price are both opened and filled without any price control enforcement.

hypotheses.title: afterSwapRefund Validates msg.sender Only — Executor-Crafted callbackData Can Redirect Refunds
hypotheses.mechanism: CLOBTransferHandler.afterSwapRefund (lines 315-333) is the AMM callback for post-swap refunds. Its only auth check is `msg.sender == amm`. The callbackData parameter arrives from the AMM, which in turn gets it from the swap hookData supplied by the executor. The callbackData is legitimately built inside ammHandleTransfer (lines 221-300) and encodes orderSeller, refundAmount, and order identifiers. If the AMM passes executor-supplied hookData through to the callback without integrity attestation (e.g., by hashing and verifying callbackData against an ammHandleTransfer-written slot), an executor can craft callbackData to redirect refunds from legitimate order sellers to themselves.
hypotheses.grounded_in: afterSwapRefund line 317: `if (msg.sender != amm) revert`. No check that callbackData was produced by this contract's ammHandleTransfer invocation for this specific swap. Requires tracing whether AMM attests callbackData between ammHandleTransfer and afterSwapRefund invocations.
hypotheses.value_extraction: If AMM passes executor-controlled bytes directly as callbackData to afterSwapRefund without attestation, executor can redirect partial fill refunds from legitimate order sellers to themselves by crafting callbackData with the attacker as orderSeller.

hypotheses.title: Asymmetric BEFORE_SWAP/AFTER_SWAP Flags Enable Stale tstore Cross-Swap Price Bypass
hypotheses.mechanism: This is a distinct exploitation vector from known M-05 (single swap with beforeSwap disabled). When BEFORE_SWAP_HOOK_FLAG (1<<0) is disabled for token X but AFTER_SWAP_HOOK_FLAG (1<<1) is enabled, and a prior swap in the same tx executed for token Y (both flags enabled), the tstore slot DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT retains Y's amount. The subsequent afterSwap for token X reads Y's amount from tstore and validates token X's price against an unrelated amount. An attacker structures a multi-swap transaction: first swap for a legitimate token writes a small 'safe' amount to tstore, then the attacker's large exploit swap for their asymmetrically flagged token has its afterSwap validate against the small safe amount — bypassing the actual price constraint.
hypotheses.grounded_in: tstore slot 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF persists for the entire transaction. If tokenX has BEFORE_SWAP disabled: beforeSwap() is not invoked for tokenX swaps, no write to tstore. If AFTER_SWAP enabled: afterSwap() IS invoked, reads stale slot written by previous swap in same tx. This cross-swap staleness is distinct from M-05's within-single-swap scenario.
hypotheses.value_extraction: Attacker's token has AFTER_SWAP enabled but BEFORE_SWAP disabled. Attacker fronts a small legitimate swap to write a favorable amount to tstore, then executes a large exploit swap. The exploit swap's afterSwap reads the small legitimate amount and passes pricing bounds, allowing extraction of value at a price the bounds were meant to prevent.

hypotheses.title: Duplicate bounds.isSet Check in validateHandlerOrder Creates Dead-Code Validation Gap
hypotheses.mechanism: AMMStandardHook.validateHandlerOrder contains two sequential `if (bounds.isSet)` blocks at lines 211 and 217. If the first block validates min price and the second validates max price (or performs a different validation), both execute when isSet=true. However if one block's body always reverts or returns before the second block is reached when isSet=true, the second check is dead code and its intended validation is silently skipped. An attacker at the exact boundary value (sqrtPrice == minSqrtPriceX96 or == maxSqrtPriceX96) may get inconsistent behavior depending on comparison operators (strict vs non-strict) and which block is reachable.
hypotheses.grounded_in: Two separate `if (bounds.isSet)` blocks at lines 211 and 217 in validateHandlerOrder. If the second block is unreachable when isSet=true (because the first block always returns or reverts in the isSet=true branch), intended validation in the second block is never exercised.
hypotheses.value_extraction: If the duplicate bounds check creates a dead-code gap, orders just below minSqrtPriceX96 may pass validation. Low severity individually; combined with other bypasses (H-handler-hook-02, H-handler-hook-04) compounds the price-validation-free window.
